column9: Thaumastoderma cantacuzeni Lévi, 1958. This new species of Thaumatoderma comes from a sample of coarse sand collected by Mr. CANTACUZENE. Cantacuzino (French: Cantacuzène) is a Romanian aristocratic family (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantacuzino_family). One prince was even a famous racing driver (see https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Ghyka_Cantacuzene). The lifetime of the latter fits to the species description...

column9: Chaetonotus lucksi Voigt, 1958 **Etymology not specified. Probably in honor of a person named Lucks. Voigt (1958) mentions a person "R. Lucks" who found specimens of C. lucksi on the underside of leafs of Nuphar lutea. I screened some publications of R. Lucks in Wilko's Rotifera-pdf-collection. And Lucks (1912) finally revealed his full name: Robert Lucks, botanical assitant at the "landwirtschaftliche Versuchsstation zu Danzig". Danzig belonged to the German Empire until the end of WWI, then it had the status of a "free city".
